reading.title: Online Classes
reading.text: More university students now take part of their course online. A student can pause a lecture and play it again, which helps when the teacher speaks quickly. However, some students miss the chance to ask a question in a real classroom. In a 2024 survey at one university in Taiwan, 62 percent of students liked the flexible timetable, but only 41 percent said they spoke enough English during online classes. The campus library is still open every weekday, and many students go there to study with friends. The university has no plan to remove face-to-face teaching.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Students can play a recorded lecture again.
qs.explanation: 文章說學生可以暫停並再播放課程，所以這句是 True。
qs.evidence: A student can pause a lecture and play it again.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Most students in the survey felt they spoke enough English online.
qs.explanation: 只有 41 percent 覺得線上英文說得夠，並非大多數，所以是 False。
qs.evidence: only 41 percent said they spoke enough English

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The survey compared three universities in Taiwan.
qs.explanation: 文章只提到 one university，沒有比較三所大學，所以是 Not Given。
qs.evidence: a 2024 survey at one university in Taiwan

qs.prompt: What did 62 percent of the students like?
qs.explanation: 62 percent 喜歡的是彈性的時間表。
qs.evidence: 62 percent of students liked the flexible timetable

qs.prompt: Where do many students study with friends?
qs.explanation: 許多學生到校園圖書館和朋友一起讀書。
qs.evidence: many students go there to study with friends

qs.prompt: What does the university plan to do about classrooms?
qs.explanation: 大學沒有打算取消面對面教學。
qs.evidence: The university has no plan to remove face-to-face teaching.

reading.title: Plastic in Daily Life
reading.text: Plastic is light and cheap, so shops use it for bags, bottles and food boxes. The problem starts after we throw it away. A plastic bottle can remain in the sea for hundreds of years, and small pieces are often eaten by fish. Some cities now charge shoppers for a plastic bag. In one coastal town, the charge cut bag use by about a third in the first year. Scientists say the charge helps, but it does not replace recycling. People still need to rinse bottles and put them in the correct bin. The article does not discuss air travel.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Plastic is popular with shops because it is light and cheap.
qs.explanation: 文章開頭就說塑膠又輕又便宜，所以商店使用它。True。
qs.evidence: Plastic is light and cheap, so shops use it

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The bag charge removed all plastic waste in the town.
qs.explanation: 收費只讓塑膠袋使用減少約三分之一，而且作者說它不能取代回收。False。
qs.evidence: the charge cut bag use by about a third

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The town banned plastic bottles last winter.
qs.explanation: 文章沒有提到禁止塑膠瓶，也沒有提到去年冬天。Not Given。

qs.prompt: What sometimes happens to small pieces of plastic?
choices: Shops reuse them the same day
qs.explanation: 小碎片常被魚吃掉。
qs.evidence: small pieces are often eaten by fish

qs.prompt: What should people do with bottles?
qs.explanation: 文章建議沖洗瓶子並放入正確的回收桶。
qs.evidence: rinse bottles and put them in the correct bin

qs.prompt: By about how much did bag use fall in the first year?
qs.explanation: 第一年大約減少三分之一。
qs.evidence: cut bag use by about a third in the first year

reading.title: Phones at Work
reading.text: A small design office in Taichung asked staff to leave personal phones in a box during meetings. The manager, Ms Lin, said meetings became twenty minutes shorter because people stopped checking messages. Not everyone agreed. Two designers said they needed the phone to show photos to a client. The office therefore allows phones when a client is in the room, but not during ordinary team meetings. The rule began in March. The company has not measured whether the quality of the design work improved.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Meetings became shorter after the phone box was introduced.
qs.explanation: 經理說會議少了二十分鐘。True。
qs.evidence: meetings became twenty minutes shorter

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Every designer supported the rule.
qs.explanation: 有兩位設計師不同意，因為他們要給客戶看照片。False。
qs.evidence: Not everyone agreed.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The design work is now better than before.
qs.explanation: 公司還沒有衡量設計品質是否變好，所以不能說已經變好。Not Given。
qs.evidence: has not measured whether the quality of the design work improved

qs.prompt: When may staff use phones?
choices: When a client is in the room
qs.explanation: 客戶在場時可以使用，一般團隊會議不行。
qs.evidence: allows phones when a client is in the room

qs.prompt: Where is the office?
qs.explanation: 辦公室在台中。
qs.evidence: A small design office in Taichung

qs.prompt: When did the rule start?
qs.explanation: 規定從三月開始。
qs.evidence: The rule began in March.

reading.title: A Short Walk
reading.text: Doctors at a city clinic advise adults to walk for thirty minutes on most days. The walk does not have to be fast. Even a walk to the market counts. Patients who walked regularly for three months reported better sleep and less back pain. The clinic did not claim that walking cures serious disease. It also reminded people with chest pain to speak to a doctor before they start. The advice is free, and the clinic prints it on a small card. No special shoes are required.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The clinic says every walk must be very fast.
qs.explanation: 文章說不必走很快。False。
qs.evidence: The walk does not have to be fast.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Some patients slept better after walking for three months.
qs.explanation: 規律走路三個月的病人回報睡眠變好。True。
qs.evidence: reported better sleep and less back pain

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The clinic sells walking shoes.
qs.explanation: 只說不需要特殊鞋子，沒有說診所賣鞋。Not Given。
qs.evidence: No special shoes are required.

qs.prompt: How long should adults try to walk on most days?
qs.explanation: 建議大多數日子走三十分鐘。
qs.evidence: walk for thirty minutes on most days

qs.prompt: Who should talk to a doctor before starting?
qs.explanation: 有胸痛的人開始前要先問醫生。
qs.evidence: people with chest pain to speak to a doctor before they start

qs.prompt: What does the clinic say walking does NOT do?
choices: Count a walk to the market
qs.explanation: 診所沒有聲稱走路能治癒嚴重疾病。
qs.evidence: did not claim that walking cures serious disease

reading.title: Working from Home
reading.text: After the office moved to a smaller building, half of the staff at GreenMart began working from home two days a week. Workers save the commute, and several said they finish reports earlier in a quiet room. The company still wants everyone in the office on Wednesday for meetings. New staff must spend their first month fully on site, so they can learn the job from a colleague. GreenMart did not cut salaries when the building became smaller. Managers say the home days are a trial until December.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：All staff work from home every day.
qs.explanation: 只有一半員工、每週兩天在家，星期三還要進辦公室。False。
qs.evidence: half of the staff ... two days a week

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：New staff stay in the office for the first month.
qs.explanation: 新員工第一個月必須全程在公司。True。
qs.evidence: New staff must spend their first month fully on site

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Staff pay is lower in the smaller building.
qs.explanation: 文章明確說薪水沒有因為大樓變小而減少。False。
qs.evidence: did not cut salaries

qs.prompt: Which day must everyone be in the office?
qs.explanation: 星期三全員進辦公室開會。
qs.evidence: everyone in the office on Wednesday

qs.prompt: Why do some workers finish reports earlier at home?
qs.explanation: 他們說安靜的房間讓報告更早完成。
qs.evidence: finish reports earlier in a quiet room

qs.prompt: How long is the home-working trial?
qs.explanation: 在家工作只是試行到十二月。
qs.evidence: a trial until December

reading.title: The New Train Line
reading.text: A new train line opened between the harbour and the university in June. The journey takes eighteen minutes, and trains run every ten minutes from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. A single ticket costs 25 dollars. Students pay 15 dollars if they show a valid student card. Bicycles are allowed only on the last carriage, and they are not allowed during the morning rush from 7:30 to 9:00. In the first month, about 40,000 people used the line. The city has not yet decided whether shops will open inside the stations.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Trains stop running at 11 p.m.
qs.explanation: 班次從早上 6 點到晚上 11 點。True。
qs.evidence: from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Students travel free.
qs.explanation: 學生票是 15 元，不是免費。False。
qs.evidence: Students pay 15 dollars

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Shops inside the stations are already open.
qs.explanation: 市府還沒決定車站裡要不要開店，所以不能說已經開了。Not Given 比 False 更準，因為連決定都還沒有。
qs.evidence: has not yet decided whether shops will open

qs.prompt: How long is the journey?
qs.explanation: 車程十八分鐘。十個月是班距，二十五是票價。
qs.evidence: The journey takes eighteen minutes

qs.prompt: When are bicycles not allowed?
qs.explanation: 早高峰 7:30 到 9:00 不能帶腳踏車。
qs.evidence: not allowed during the morning rush from 7:30 to 9:00

qs.prompt: How many people used the line in the first month?
qs.explanation: 第一個月大約四萬人。
qs.evidence: about 40,000 people used the line

reading.title: An Older Town
reading.text: The town of Hualien's fishing district has fewer children than it did twenty years ago. Many young adults move to bigger cities for work, so the local school now has only four classes. The clinic, however, is busier, because a larger share of residents are over sixty. Volunteers run a lunch club three times a week. The mayor wants to build small flats for older people near the clinic, but the plan still needs funding. The passage does not say that the school will close. Tourism in summer remains important for shops on the main street.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：There are fewer children in the district than twenty years ago.
qs.explanation: 文章第一句就說孩子比二十年前少。True。
qs.evidence: has fewer children than it did twenty years ago

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The school has already closed.
qs.explanation: 學校還在，只是只剩四個班，文章也說沒有提到會關閉。False。
qs.evidence: the local school now has only four classes

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The new flats have already been built.
qs.explanation: 市長想蓋，但還需要經費，沒有說已經蓋好。Not Given。
qs.evidence: the plan still needs funding

qs.prompt: Why is the clinic busier?
qs.explanation: 因為超過六十歲的居民比例變高。
qs.evidence: a larger share of residents are over sixty

qs.prompt: How often does the lunch club meet?
qs.explanation: 志工的午餐會每週三次。
qs.evidence: a lunch club three times a week

qs.prompt: What remains important for shops on the main street?
qs.explanation: 夏天的觀光對大街商店仍然重要。
qs.evidence: Tourism in summer remains important

reading.title: A Free Museum
reading.text: The city museum stopped charging for entry on weekdays. Visitor numbers rose from 800 a day to about 2,000. Teachers bring classes on Tuesday morning, when the galleries are quieter. The most popular room shows old photographs of the harbour. Audio guides are available in Mandarin and English, but not in Japanese. A small shop sells postcards, and the money from the shop helps pay for school visits. The museum is closed on Monday for cleaning. Cameras are allowed, but flash is not.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Entry is free on weekdays.
qs.explanation: 平日停止收費，所以平日免費。True。
qs.evidence: stopped charging for entry on weekdays

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Audio guides include Japanese.
qs.explanation: 語音導覽有中文和英文，但沒有日文。False。
qs.evidence: in Mandarin and English, but not in Japanese

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The photographs were taken by a famous artist.
qs.explanation: 只說最受歡迎的房間有舊港照片，沒有說拍攝者。Not Given。
qs.evidence: old photographs of the harbour

qs.prompt: About how many people visit each day now?
qs.explanation: 人數從每天 800 升到大約 2,000。
qs.evidence: rose from 800 a day to about 2,000

qs.prompt: When is the museum closed?
qs.explanation: 星期一清掃，不開放。
qs.evidence: closed on Monday for cleaning

qs.prompt: What helps pay for school visits?
qs.explanation: 商店賣明信片的收入用來支付學校參觀。
qs.evidence: the money from the shop helps pay for school visits

reading.title: Lunch at School
reading.text: A secondary school changed its lunch menu in September. Fried food is served only on Friday, and students can choose fruit instead of a sweet drink. After one term, the canteen sold 30 percent fewer soft drinks. Teachers noticed that afternoon classes were a little calmer, but they did not prove that the menu was the only reason. Some parents complained that the new meals cost 10 dollars more each week. The school kitchen still uses local vegetables when they are in season. Breakfast is not provided.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Fried food is available every day.
qs.explanation: 油炸食物只在星期五供應。False。
qs.evidence: Fried food is served only on Friday

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Soft drink sales fell by about 30 percent.
qs.explanation: 一學期後汽水少賣了百分之三十。True。
qs.evidence: sold 30 percent fewer soft drinks

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The calmer classes were caused only by the new menu.
qs.explanation: 老師沒有證明菜單是唯一原因，所以不能說只是因為菜單。False。
qs.evidence: did not prove that the menu was the only reason

qs.prompt: What can students choose instead of a sweet drink?
qs.explanation: 可以用水果代替甜飲料。
qs.evidence: choose fruit instead of a sweet drink

qs.prompt: Why did some parents complain?
choices: Meals cost 10 dollars more a week
qs.explanation: 新餐點每週貴了 10 元。
qs.evidence: the new meals cost 10 dollars more each week

qs.prompt: What is not provided?
qs.explanation: 學校不提供早餐。
qs.evidence: Breakfast is not provided.

reading.title: Renting near Campus
reading.text: Rents near the campus rose by 15 percent last year. A single room now costs about 8,000 dollars a month, not including electricity. Many students share a flat so that each person pays less. The university keeps 200 low-cost beds, but the waiting list is long, and first-year students are given priority. Landlords must return the deposit within two weeks if the room is left in good condition. The city is building a new dormitory, yet it will not open until the year after next. Cafes near the gate have also become more expensive.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：A single room costs about 8,000 dollars a month before electricity.
qs.explanation: 單人房大約每月 8,000，電費另計。True。
qs.evidence: about 8,000 dollars a month, not including electricity

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Any student can get a low-cost bed immediately.
qs.explanation: 候補名單很長，而且一年級優先，不是任何人立刻有床。False。
qs.evidence: the waiting list is long, and first-year students are given priority

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The new dormitory opens this September.
qs.explanation: 要後年才開，不是今年九月。False。
qs.evidence: will not open until the year after next

qs.prompt: By how much did rents rise last year?
qs.explanation: 去年租金上漲百分之十五。
qs.evidence: rose by 15 percent last year

qs.prompt: When must a landlord return the deposit?
choices: Within two weeks if the room is in good condition
qs.explanation: 房間狀況良好時，兩週內退還押金。
qs.evidence: return the deposit within two weeks

qs.prompt: What else near the campus became more expensive?
qs.explanation: 校門口的咖啡店也變貴了。
qs.evidence: Cafes near the gate have also become more expensive.

reading.title: Rooftop Solar
reading.text: The town fitted solar panels on the roof of the sports hall in April. On sunny days the panels produce enough electricity for the lights and the showers. They do not power the whole town. Extra power is sold to the grid, and the income pays for repairs. In cloudy weeks the hall still uses ordinary electricity. Engineers check the panels twice a year. Local schools visit in May to learn how the system works. The project cost 2 million dollars and was partly funded by a national grant. Wind power is not used at the hall.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The panels can supply the whole town.
qs.explanation: 文章說它們不能供應整個城鎮。False。
qs.evidence: They do not power the whole town.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：Extra electricity is sold.
qs.explanation: 多餘的電賣給電網，收入用來維修。True。
qs.evidence: Extra power is sold to the grid

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：The panels were made in Taiwan.
qs.explanation: 沒有提到面板的製造地。Not Given。

qs.prompt: When were the panels fitted?
qs.explanation: 四月裝在體育館屋頂。五月是學校參觀。
qs.evidence: fitted solar panels ... in April

qs.prompt: What happens in cloudy weeks?
qs.explanation: 陰天那幾週仍使用一般電力。
qs.evidence: In cloudy weeks the hall still uses ordinary electricity.

qs.prompt: How was the project paid for in part?
qs.explanation: 部分經費來自國家補助。風電並沒有用在這座館。
qs.evidence: partly funded by a national grant

reading.title: Preparing for a Speaking Test
reading.text: James practises IELTS speaking for fifteen minutes every evening. He records himself and listens the next morning. His teacher told him to answer the question first and then give one reason and one example. Long lists of hard words do not help if the answer is unclear. In Part 2 he now spends the one minute of preparation writing three short prompts, not full sentences. He still finds Part 3 difficult because the questions are more general. He has not taken the real test yet. His target is band 6.5, and the test date on his form is 7 June 2027.

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：James practises speaking every evening.
qs.explanation: 他每天晚上練習十五分鐘。True。
qs.evidence: practises IELTS speaking for fifteen minutes every evening

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：His teacher wants him to begin with a long list of difficult words.
qs.explanation: 老師要他先回答，再給一個理由和一個例子。難字清單如果讓答案不清楚就沒有幫助。False。
qs.evidence: answer the question first and then give one reason and one example

qs.prompt: 根據文章判斷：James scored 6.5 on a test last month.
qs.explanation: 6.5 是目標，他還沒考正式考試，文章沒有說他上個月考了 6.5。Not Given。
qs.evidence: He has not taken the real test yet.

qs.prompt: What does he write during the Part 2 preparation minute?
qs.explanation: 他現在只寫三個短提示，不寫完整句子。
qs.evidence: writing three short prompts, not full sentences

qs.prompt: Which part is still hard for him?
qs.explanation: 他仍覺得 Part 3 較難，因為問題比較概括。
qs.evidence: He still finds Part 3 difficult

qs.prompt: When is the test date on his form?
qs.explanation: 表格上的考試日是 2027 年 6 月 7 日。
qs.evidence: the test date on his form is 7 June 2027

listening.audio: Please submit the essay by Friday.
listening.prompt: Please ______ the essay by Friday.
listening.explanation: submit 是繳交。admit 承認，permit 允許，omit 省略。

listening.audio: The library is closed on Monday.
listening.prompt: The library is ______ on Monday.
listening.explanation: be closed 表示關閉。這裡是形容詞 closed。

listening.audio: She has lived here since 2019.
listening.prompt: She has lived here ______ 2019.
listening.explanation: since 接一個起點，for 接一段時間。

listening.audio: We have studied English for six years.
listening.prompt: We have studied English ______ six years.
listening.explanation: for 後面接地點以外的一段時間。

listening.audio: He is interested in history.
listening.prompt: He is interested ______ history.
listening.explanation: interested 的介系詞是 in。

listening.audio: Success depends on regular practice.
listening.prompt: Success depends ______ regular practice.
listening.explanation: depend on 表示取決於。

listening.audio: I look forward to hearing from you.
listening.prompt: I look forward to ______ from you.
listening.explanation: look forward to 的 to 是介系詞，後面用 V-ing。

listening.audio: There was a significant increase in rent.
listening.prompt: There was a significant ______ in rent.
listening.explanation: increase 是增加。decrease 是減少。

listening.audio: The number of cars has doubled.
listening.prompt: The ______ of cars has doubled.
listening.explanation: 可數名詞 cars 用 the number of。

listening.audio: A number of students were absent.
listening.prompt: A number of students ______ absent.
listening.explanation: a number of 表示許多，動詞用複數。

listening.audio: Despite the rain, the match continued.
listening.prompt: ______ the rain, the match continued.
listening.explanation: Despite 後面接受詞 the rain，Although 要接子句。

listening.audio: Although it was late, she kept working.
listening.prompt: ______ it was late, she kept working.
listening.explanation: Although 後面有主詞 it 和動詞 was。

listening.audio: The price rose by five pounds.
listening.prompt: The price rose ______ five pounds.
listening.explanation: 上升的幅度用 by。

listening.audio: Compared with buses, trains are quicker.
listening.prompt: ______ with buses, trains are quicker.
listening.explanation: Compared with 表示與…相比。

listening.audio: If I had more time, I would travel.
listening.prompt: If I ______ more time, I would travel.
listening.explanation: 與現在事實相反，If 後面用過去式 had。

listening.audio: Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.
listening.prompt: Hardly ______ down when the phone rang.
listening.explanation: Hardly 放句首要倒裝：Hardly had I ...

listening.audio: You should have revised more.
listening.prompt: You ______ revised more.
listening.explanation: 過去該做卻沒做：should have + 過去分詞。

listening.audio: The bridge was built in 1998.
listening.prompt: The bridge ______ in 1998.
listening.explanation: 過去的被動是 was / were + 過去分詞。

listening.audio: English is spoken in many countries.
listening.prompt: English ______ in many countries.
listening.explanation: 現在被動：is / are + 過去分詞。

listening.audio: Each of the answers is correct.
listening.prompt: Each of the answers ______ correct.
listening.explanation: Each of 的動詞用單數。

listening.audio: The news was surprising.
listening.prompt: The news ______ surprising.
listening.explanation: news 是不可數，動詞用單數。

listening.audio: I prefer tea to coffee.
listening.prompt: I prefer tea ______ coffee.
listening.explanation: prefer A to B，不用 than。

listening.audio: She enjoys reading in the evening.
listening.prompt: She enjoys ______ in the evening.
listening.explanation: enjoy 後面用 V-ing。

listening.audio: They decided to cancel the trip.
listening.prompt: They decided ______ the trip.
listening.explanation: decide 後面用 to + 原形。

listening.audio: I am used to getting up early.
listening.prompt: I am used to ______ up early.
listening.explanation: be used to 後面用 V-ing，表示習慣於。

listening.audio: I used to live in Taichung.
listening.prompt: I ______ live in Taichung.
listening.explanation: used to + 原形，表示過去的習慣。

listening.audio: It was so boring that we left.
listening.prompt: It was ______ boring that we left.
listening.explanation: so + 形容詞 + that。

listening.audio: It was such a hot day that we stayed in.
listening.prompt: It was ______ a hot day that we stayed in.
listening.explanation: such a + 形容詞 + 名詞。

listening.audio: I wish I had more free time.
listening.prompt: I wish I ______ more free time.
listening.explanation: wish 後面用過去式，表示現在做不到的願望。

listening.audio: He said he would call the next day.
listening.prompt: He said he ______ call the next day.
listening.explanation: 轉述時 will 改成 would。

listening.audio: Look at those clouds. It is going to rain.
listening.prompt: Look at those clouds. It ______ rain.
listening.explanation: 有眼前證據的預測用 be going to。

listening.audio: Could you give me some information?
listening.prompt: Could you give me ______ information?
listening.explanation: information 不可數，不能加 a。

listening.audio: She gave me a piece of advice.
listening.prompt: She gave me a ______ of advice.
listening.explanation: advice 不可數，要說 a piece of advice。

listening.audio: How much money do you need?
listening.prompt: How ______ money do you need?
listening.explanation: money 不可數，用 much。

listening.audio: There were fewer people than yesterday.
listening.prompt: There were ______ people than yesterday.
listening.explanation: people 可數，用 fewer，不用 less。

listening.audio: The hotel was expensive. However, the view was wonderful.
listening.prompt: The hotel was expensive. ______, the view was wonderful.
listening.explanation: However 連接兩個句子，後面加逗號。

listening.audio: In spite of being tired, she kept working.
listening.prompt: ______ being tired, she kept working.
listening.explanation: in spite of 後面用 V-ing 或名詞。沒有 despite of。

listening.audio: Not only did she pass, but she also won a prize.
listening.prompt: Not only ______ the exam, but she also won a prize.
listening.explanation: Not only 放句首要倒裝。

listening.audio: Under no circumstances should you share your password.
listening.prompt: Under no circumstances ______ your password.
listening.explanation: 否定片語放句首要倒裝。

listening.audio: The form must be completed in black ink.
listening.prompt: The form must ______ in black ink.
listening.explanation: 情態動詞的被動是 must be + 過去分詞。

listening.audio: The teacher who taught me has retired.
listening.prompt: The teacher ______ taught me has retired.
listening.explanation: 人當主詞用 who。

listening.audio: This is the cafe where we first met.
listening.prompt: This is the cafe ______ we first met.
listening.explanation: 地方用 where。

listening.audio: I have a friend whose brother studies in London.
listening.prompt: I have a friend ______ brother studies in London.
listening.explanation: whose 表示誰的，後面接名詞。

listening.audio: By the time we arrived, the train had left.
listening.prompt: By the time we arrived, the train ______.
listening.explanation: 更早完成的動作用 had + 過去分詞。

listening.audio: It has been raining all morning.
listening.prompt: It ______ all morning.
listening.explanation: 從過去持續到現在，用現在完成進行式。

listening.audio: I saw this film two years ago.
listening.prompt: I ______ this film two years ago.
listening.explanation: ago 用過去簡單式。

listening.audio: This question is more difficult than the last one.
listening.prompt: This question is ______ than the last one.
listening.explanation: 多音節形容詞用 more，不加 -er。

listening.audio: The more you practise, the more confident you become.
listening.prompt: ______ you practise, the more confident you become.
listening.explanation: the + 比較級, the + 比較級。

listening.audio: My parents let me stay out late.
listening.prompt: My parents let me ______ out late.
listening.explanation: let 後面用原形，不加 to。

listening.audio: The news made her happy.
listening.prompt: The news made her ______.
listening.explanation: make + 受詞 + 形容詞。

listening.audio: She is good at explaining ideas.
listening.prompt: She is good ______ explaining ideas.
listening.explanation: good at + V-ing。

listening.audio: We need to decide whether to accept the offer.
listening.prompt: We need to decide ______ to accept the offer.
listening.explanation: 不確定要不要，用 whether。

listening.audio: What surprised me was the price.
listening.prompt: ______ surprised me was the price.
listening.explanation: What 引導名詞子句，表示所…的事物。

listening.audio: They must have gone home. The lights are off.
listening.prompt: They ______ home. The lights are off.
listening.explanation: 對過去很有把握的推測：must have + 過去分詞。

listening.audio: He can't have received the email, because he was on a plane.
listening.prompt: He ______ the email, because he was on a plane.
listening.explanation: 對過去的否定推測：can't have + 過去分詞。

listening.audio: Recycling is collected every Tuesday.
listening.prompt: Recycling ______ every Tuesday.
listening.explanation: 回收物被收取，用被動。

listening.audio: The majority of the students are in favour.
listening.prompt: The majority of the students ______ in favour.
listening.explanation: the majority of + 複數名詞，動詞常用複數。

listening.audio: Neither of the options is suitable.
listening.prompt: Neither of the options ______ suitable.
listening.explanation: Neither of 正式用法動詞用單數。

listening.audio: There is a serious problem with the data.
listening.prompt: There ______ a serious problem with the data.
listening.explanation: problem 是單數，There is。

listening.audio: People in this town are very friendly.
listening.prompt: People in this town ______ very friendly.
listening.explanation: people 表示人們時用複數動詞。

listening.audio: Woman: The seminar was at two, but it's been moved to half past three. Man: OK, I'll come at 3:30.
listening.prompt: What time will the man come?
listening.explanation: 原本兩點，改到三點半，男生說他 3:30 到。

listening.audio: Man: Did you take the bus? Woman: No, I walked. It only took twenty minutes.
listening.prompt: How did the woman travel?
listening.explanation: 她說她走路。on foot 就是步行。

listening.audio: Woman: The library closes at seven tonight. Man: Then we should leave here by six.
listening.prompt: When does the library close tonight?
listening.explanation: 女生說圖書館七點關。六點是他們要離開的時間。

listening.audio: Man: Is the museum free on Monday? Woman: Monday it's closed. It's free on Tuesday.
listening.prompt: When is the museum free?
listening.explanation: 星期一公休，星期二免費。

listening.audio: Woman: I used to drink coffee every morning. Man: And now? Woman: I drink tea instead.
listening.prompt: What does the woman drink now?
listening.explanation: 她現在改喝茶。used to 是過去。

listening.audio: Man: How long have you lived here? Woman: Since 2019. Before that I was in Taichung.
listening.prompt: When did the woman start living here?
listening.explanation: since 2019 表示從 2019 開始住在這裡。

listening.audio: Woman: The report hasn't been finished yet. Man: The manager wants it by Friday.
listening.prompt: What is true about the report?
listening.explanation: hasn't been finished yet 表示還沒完成。

listening.audio: Man: Should I take an umbrella? Woman: Yes. Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
listening.prompt: Why should the man take an umbrella?
listening.explanation: 女生根據烏雲判斷快下雨了。

listening.audio: Woman: A single room is 8,000 a month, not including electricity. Man: That's more than I expected.
listening.prompt: What is NOT included in the 8,000?
listening.explanation: 8,000 不含電費。

listening.audio: Man: Did everyone agree with the phone rule? Woman: No. Two designers needed their phones for clients.
listening.prompt: How many designers disagreed in the example?
listening.explanation: 有兩位設計師需要手機給客戶看照片。

listening.audio: Woman: Trains run every ten minutes until 11 p.m. Man: The journey is only eighteen minutes.
listening.prompt: How often do the trains run?
listening.explanation: 每十分鐘一班。十八分鐘是車程。

listening.audio: Man: Students pay 15 dollars if they show a student card. Woman: A normal ticket is 25.
listening.prompt: How much is a student ticket?
listening.explanation: 學生票 15 元，一般票 25 元。

listening.audio: Woman: Bicycles are not allowed between 7:30 and 9:00. Man: I'll take the later train then.
listening.prompt: When are bicycles banned?
listening.explanation: 早高峰 7:30 到 9:00 不能帶車。

listening.audio: Man: Fried food is only on Friday now. Woman: And soft drink sales fell by 30 percent.
listening.prompt: When can students eat fried food?
listening.explanation: 油炸食物只在星期五。

listening.audio: Woman: The clinic advises a thirty-minute walk on most days. Man: Does it have to be fast? Woman: No.
listening.prompt: Must the walk be fast?
listening.explanation: 文章式對話明確說不必走很快。

listening.audio: Man: Half the staff work from home two days a week. Woman: But Wednesday everyone comes in.
listening.prompt: Which day is everyone in the office?
listening.explanation: 星期三全員進公司。

listening.audio: Woman: New staff stay on site for the first month. Man: So they can learn from a colleague.
listening.prompt: Why do new staff stay in the office?
listening.explanation: 第一個月在公司是為了跟同事學工作。

listening.audio: Man: The solar panels do not power the whole town. Woman: But they run the lights and the showers on sunny days.
listening.prompt: What can the panels do on sunny days?
listening.explanation: 晴天足夠供應燈和淋浴，不是整個城鎮。

listening.audio: Woman: Visitor numbers rose from 800 to about 2,000 a day. Man: After entry became free on weekdays? Woman: Yes.
listening.prompt: About how many people visit each day now?
listening.explanation: 現在大約每天 2,000 人。800 是之前。

listening.audio: Man: The museum is closed on Monday. Woman: Then let's go on Tuesday morning. It's quieter.
listening.prompt: Why does the woman suggest Tuesday morning?
listening.explanation: 她說星期二早上比較安靜。

listening.audio: Woman: Audio guides are in Mandarin and English, but not Japanese. Man: That's fine. I need English.
listening.prompt: Which language is NOT available?
listening.explanation: 沒有日文導覽。

listening.audio: Man: Rents rose by 15 percent. Woman: A room is about 8,000, and cafes got more expensive too.
listening.prompt: What rose by 15 percent?
listening.explanation: 上漲 15% 的是租金。

listening.audio: Woman: First-year students get priority for the cheap beds. Man: The waiting list is long.
listening.prompt: Who is given priority?
listening.explanation: 一年級學生優先。

listening.audio: Man: The deposit must be returned within two weeks. Woman: Only if the room is in good condition.
listening.prompt: When is the deposit returned?
choices: Within two weeks if the room is fine
listening.explanation: 房間狀況良好才在兩週內退押金。

listening.audio: Woman: I record myself and listen the next morning. Man: How long do you practise? Woman: Fifteen minutes every evening.
listening.prompt: When does she listen to the recording?
listening.explanation: 她隔天早上聽自己的錄音。

listening.audio: Man: In Part 2 I write three short prompts, not full sentences. Woman: And Part 3? Man: Still hard.
listening.prompt: What does the man write in the preparation minute?
listening.explanation: 他只寫三個短提示。

listening.audio: Woman: The university will not remove face-to-face teaching. Man: Good. I miss asking questions in class.
listening.prompt: What will the university keep?
listening.explanation: 大學不會取消面對面教學。

listening.audio: Man: Only 41 percent said they spoke enough English online. Woman: But 62 percent liked the flexible timetable.
listening.prompt: What did 62 percent like?
listening.explanation: 62% 喜歡彈性課表。41% 才是覺得英文說得夠。

listening.audio: Woman: A plastic bottle can stay in the sea for hundreds of years. Man: And fish eat the small pieces.
listening.prompt: What eats small pieces of plastic?
listening.explanation: 小碎片常被魚吃掉。

listening.audio: Man: The bag charge cut use by about a third. Woman: It still doesn't replace recycling.
listening.prompt: What does the woman say the charge cannot replace?
listening.explanation: 收費有幫助，但不能取代回收。

listening.audio: Woman: Please rinse the bottles before you recycle them. Man: And put them in the correct bin.
listening.prompt: What should you do before recycling bottles?
listening.explanation: 回收前要先沖洗。

listening.audio: Man: Meetings became twenty minutes shorter. Woman: Because people stopped checking messages? Man: Yes.
listening.prompt: Why were meetings shorter?
listening.explanation: 大家不再看訊息，會議少了二十分鐘。

listening.audio: Woman: Phones are allowed when a client is in the room. Man: But not in ordinary team meetings.
listening.prompt: When are phones allowed?
listening.explanation: 客戶在場才可以用。

listening.audio: Man: Patients who walked for three months slept better. Woman: Did the clinic say walking cures disease? Man: No.
listening.prompt: What did walkers report?
listening.explanation: 他們回報睡眠變好，但診所沒說能治癒重病。

listening.audio: Woman: People with chest pain should speak to a doctor first. Man: The advice card is free.
listening.prompt: Who should see a doctor before starting?
listening.explanation: 有胸痛的人要先問醫生。

listening.audio: Man: About 40,000 people used the new line in the first month. Woman: And bikes only in the last carriage.
listening.prompt: Where may bicycles go?
listening.explanation: 腳踏車只能放最後一節車廂。

listening.audio: Woman: The lunch club meets three times a week. Man: Volunteers run it.
listening.prompt: Who runs the lunch club?
listening.explanation: 志工經營午餐會。

listening.audio: Man: The mayor wants small flats near the clinic, but the plan needs funding. Woman: So nothing is built yet.
listening.prompt: What does the plan still need?
listening.explanation: 計畫還需要經費，所以還沒蓋。

listening.audio: Woman: Summer tourism is still important for the main street shops. Man: Even though the town is older.
listening.prompt: What is still important for the shops?
listening.explanation: 夏天的觀光仍然重要。

listening.audio: Man: The school has four classes now. Woman: It has not closed.
listening.prompt: What is true about the school?
listening.explanation: 學校還在，只剩四個班。

writing.example: The city is exciting. On the other hand, it is noisy.
writing.explanation: on the other hand 是固定片語，不用 in the other hand。

writing.example: In terms of cost, the train is cheaper.
writing.explanation: in terms of 後面接名詞，表示在某方面。

writing.example: I walk every day; for instance, I walk to the market.
writing.explanation: for instance 和 for example 相近，不能說 for instants。

writing.example: The bus was full. As a result, I was late.
writing.explanation: as a result 後面常接一個結果句。

writing.example: The flat is small. In addition, it is far from the metro.
writing.explanation: in addition 後面可加逗號，再接一個句子。

writing.example: On balance, the advantages outweigh the drawbacks.
writing.explanation: on balance 表示整體衡量之後。

writing.example: From my point of view, daily practice matters most.
writing.explanation: point of view 不用 point of views。

writing.example: To a certain extent, I agree with that idea.
writing.explanation: extent 這裡是不可數的程度，不用 extents。

writing.example: I am busy, that is to say I have little free time.
writing.explanation: that is to say 用來換一種說法。

writing.example: Traffic is worse. A case in point is the morning rush.
writing.explanation: a case in point 表示正是一個例子。

writing.example: It is widely believed that exercise improves mood.
writing.explanation: widely believed 表示很多人都這樣認為。

writing.example: Parents play an important role in a child's reading.
writing.explanation: role 用 play，不用 do a role。

writing.example: Poor sleep can lead to poor concentration.
writing.explanation: lead to 後面接名詞或 V-ing，to 是介系詞。

writing.example: The delay resulted in a missed flight.
writing.explanation: result in 後面是結果。result from 後面是原因。

writing.example: His tiredness resulted from a lack of sleep.
writing.explanation: result from 表示由…造成。

writing.example: He is not only a teacher but also a writer.
writing.explanation: 兩邊詞性要對稱。

writing.example: Despite the rain, we went out.
writing.explanation: despite 後面接名詞，不接完整子句。

writing.example: Although the course was hard, she enjoyed it.
writing.explanation: although 後面要有主詞和動詞。

writing.example: The flat is tiny. In other words, there is only one room.
writing.explanation: in other words 用來改寫前一句。

writing.example: The job is tiring. At the same time, it is well paid.
writing.explanation: at the same time 可表示同時，也可輕微轉折。

writing.example: An increasing number of students study online.
writing.explanation: number of 接可數複數。

writing.example: A significant amount of money was invested.
writing.explanation: amount of 接不可數名詞。

writing.example: The government should take measures to cut pollution.
writing.explanation: measures 用 take，不用 do measures。

writing.example: The plan raised concern among local residents.
writing.explanation: concern 這裡不可數，raise concern 是引起擔憂。

writing.example: To a large extent, the result depends on practice.
writing.explanation: extent 不用 extend。extend 是動詞。

writing.example: On balance, the advantages outweigh the drawbacks.
writing.explanation: outweigh 是一個詞，表示超過。

writing.example: In the long run, walking saves money.
writing.explanation: in the long run 表示長期而言。

writing.example: There is no denying that the city is crowded.
writing.explanation: denying 是 V-ing，that 後面接子句。

writing.example: There is good reason to believe the plan will work.
writing.explanation: reason 後面用 to + 原形。
choices: there is a good reason for to

writing.example: Generally speaking, people prefer a short commute.
writing.explanation: generally speaking 是獨立片語，後面加逗號。

writing.example: To be honest, I use my phone all day.
writing.explanation: to be honest 用來坦白轉折。

writing.example: The thing is, I do not have enough time.
writing.explanation: 口說裡 the thing is 用來點出重點。

writing.example: The main reason is that big cities offer more jobs.
writing.explanation: reason 後面用 that 子句，不直接接 because。

writing.example: The rent is high. On top of that, the flat is noisy.
writing.explanation: on top of that 表示還有另一個問題或理由。

writing.example: He overslept. As a consequence, he missed the bus.
writing.explanation: consequence 是結果，拼法不是 consequense。

writing.example: Cities are noisy. By contrast, the town is quiet.
writing.explanation: by contrast 用來對比前一句。

writing.example: I do not hate the city. On the contrary, I enjoy it.
writing.explanation: on the contrary 反駁前面的說法。

writing.example: I like quiet cafes, whereas my brother likes crowds.
writing.explanation: whereas 連接兩個對比的子句。

writing.example: She set an alarm so that she would not oversleep.
writing.explanation: so that 後面接完整子句，表示目的。

writing.example: He spoke slowly in order to be clear.
writing.explanation: in order to 後面接原形動詞。

writing.example: Take the stairs instead of the lift.
writing.explanation: instead of 後面接名詞或 V-ing。

writing.example: Leave now; otherwise you will miss the train.
writing.explanation: otherwise 表示如果不這樣。

writing.example: We eventually found a quiet cafe.
writing.explanation: eventually 是最後、終於，不是 eventfully。

writing.example: I am currently preparing for IELTS.
writing.explanation: currently 常與現在進行式一起用。

writing.example: I recently started reading every day.
writing.explanation: recently 常配現在完成式或過去式。

writing.example: It is hard, especially at the beginning.
writing.explanation: especially 用來強調其中一個情況。

writing.example: I like the city, particularly the food.
writing.explanation: particularly 和 especially 接近。

writing.example: The exam was relatively fair.
writing.explanation: relatively 表示跟別的情況比起來。

writing.example: I hardly had time to eat breakfast.
writing.explanation: hardly 本身已是否定，不再加 not。

writing.example: It is nearly eight o'clock.
writing.explanation: nearly 表示差不多，接近。

writing.example: Students tend to forget irregular verbs.
writing.explanation: tend to + 原形，表示有…的傾向。

writing.example: A lack of sleep makes it hard to study.
writing.explanation: a lack of + 名詞。lack 這裡是名詞。

writing.example: Not every student has access to a quiet desk.
writing.explanation: access 後面用 to，不用 access of。

writing.example: One solution to the problem is a time limit.
writing.explanation: solution 後面用 to，不用 solution of the problem 在這個考試片語裡較不自然。

writing.example: The school will implement the new rule in March.
writing.explanation: implement 是動詞，名詞是 implementation。

writing.example: Teachers should encourage students to speak.
writing.explanation: encourage + 人 + to + 原形。

writing.example: A break can prevent you from getting too tired.
writing.explanation: prevent + 人 + from + V-ing。

writing.example: The campaign will promote cycling.
writing.explanation: promote + 名詞或 V-ing，表示推廣。

writing.example: We can reduce waste by bringing a bottle.
writing.explanation: reduce + 名詞。英式讀音是 /rɪˈdjuːs/。

writing.example: Reading aloud can improve your rhythm.
writing.explanation: improve 後面直接接受詞，不說 improve up。

writing.example: Everyone can contribute to the project.
writing.explanation: contribute to 的 to 是介系詞。

writing.example: The result will depend on how often you practise.
writing.explanation: depend 用 on，不用 depend of。

writing.example: The job will require clear spoken English.
writing.explanation: require + 名詞，或 require somebody to do。

writing.example: The course will provide you with feedback.
writing.explanation: 也可以說 provide feedback for you。with 接所提供的東西。

writing.example: Most students are in favour of the change.
writing.explanation: in favour of 是英式拼法，表示贊成。

writing.example: Some residents are opposed to the new road.
writing.explanation: opposed to 的 to 後面接名詞或 V-ing。

writing.example: Many people regard the park as the heart of the town.
writing.explanation: regard A as B，as 不能省。

writing.example: There appears to be a mistake in the total.
writing.explanation: there appears to be 比 there seems a 更完整。

writing.example: Tickets remain expensive in the holidays.
writing.explanation: remain + 形容詞，不加 to be 也可以。

writing.example: I agree with the first point.
writing.explanation: agree with + 人／看法。agree to + 提議。
choices: I agree to the point of him

writing.example: I disagree with the idea that homework is useless.
writing.explanation: disagree 後面用 with。

writing.example: Some people argue that cities are too crowded.
writing.explanation: argue that 後面接完整句子。

writing.example: I suggest taking the bus instead of a taxi.
writing.explanation: suggest 後面用 V-ing，不接 to V。

writing.example: The museum is worth the ticket price.
writing.explanation: worth 後面接名詞或 V-ing，不加 to。

writing.example: I prefer tea to coffee.
writing.explanation: prefer 名詞時用 to，不用 than。

writing.example: I recommend the night market to every visitor.
writing.explanation: recommend A to B，或 recommend doing。

writing.example: It took a few days to adapt to the food.
writing.explanation: adapt to 表示適應。adopt 是收養或採納，不要混。

writing.example: You can adjust to the new timetable.
writing.explanation: adjust to + 名詞。

writing.example: I am familiar with this street.
writing.explanation: familiar with + 事物。事物 familiar to + 人。

writing.example: Travel can broaden your horizons.
writing.explanation: horizons 常用複數。

writing.example: One advantage of the train is the view.
writing.explanation: advantage of + 名詞。

writing.example: One drawback of flying is the cost.
writing.explanation: drawback 是可數名詞，一個缺點用 one drawback。

writing.example: Reading a timetable in another language can pose a challenge.
writing.explanation: pose a challenge 表示構成挑戰。

writing.example: The trip is an opportunity to use English.
writing.explanation: opportunity to + 原形。

writing.example: Climate change is a global problem.
writing.explanation: global 是形容詞，直接放在名詞前。

writing.example: A domestic flight is often shorter than the train.
writing.explanation: domestic 可指國內的，也可指家庭的。

writing.example: The airport has many international flights.
writing.explanation: international 中間沒有 a。

writing.example: The hostel is affordable for students.
writing.explanation: affordable 是形容詞。afford 是動詞。

writing.example: Our plans are flexible if the weather changes.
writing.explanation: flexible 表示可以調整。

writing.example: Travelling alone made him more independent.
writing.explanation: independent 後面若接事物用 of：independent of。

writing.example: Short daily practice is more effective than one long session.
writing.explanation: effective 是有效果。efficient 是有效率。

writing.example: We need a practical plan, not only a hope.
writing.explanation: practical 表示做得到。

writing.example: A realistic goal keeps you going.
writing.explanation: realistic 不是 realitic。

writing.example: It is necessary to read the question twice.
writing.explanation: necessary 的英式讀音是 /ˈnesəsəri/。

writing.example: This topic is suitable for a two-minute answer.
writing.explanation: suitable for + 名詞。

writing.example: The book is available at the library.
writing.explanation: available 表示找得到、用得到。

writing.example: Sleep is crucial before an exam.
writing.explanation: crucial 後面可用 to 或 for。

writing.example: Handwashing is vital in a hospital.
writing.explanation: vital 表示不可或缺。

writing.example: There was a significant increase in sales.
writing.explanation: significant 是顯著的，不是 signature。

writing.example: The journey takes roughly forty minutes.
writing.explanation: roughly 表示大約，和 approximately 接近。

writing.example: Approximately half of the class walks to school.
writing.explanation: approximately 比 about 更正式，適合寫作。

writing.example: The number of visitors rose dramatically.
writing.explanation: dramatically 強調幅度很大。

writing.example: The town has gradually become more crowded.
writing.explanation: gradually 表示一點一點地。

writing.example: Unemployment fell sharply after the factory opened.
writing.explanation: sharply 可形容數字突然上升或下降。

writing.example: Wages have risen steadily for five years.
writing.explanation: steadily 表示穩定、沒有大波動。

writing.example: The figure is slightly higher than last year.
writing.explanation: slightly 表示只有一點點。

writing.example: Oil prices fluctuate from month to month.
writing.explanation: fluctuate 是動詞。名詞是 fluctuation。

writing.example: A large proportion of the budget goes to schools.
writing.explanation: proportion of 後面的動詞看名詞的單複數。

writing.example: The majority of students travel by bus.
writing.explanation: the majority of + 複數名詞時，動詞常用複數。

writing.example: Only a minority of residents opposed the park.
writing.explanation: minority 是少數，不是 minor。

writing.example: There is clear evidence that sleep improves memory.
writing.explanation: evidence 不可數，不說 an evidence。

writing.example: According to the chart, sales fell in May.
writing.explanation: according to 後面接名詞，不接句子當主詞。

writing.example: As the graph shows, the figure rose after 2010.
writing.explanation: as the graph shows 是插入的方式，動詞用 shows。

writing.example: Sales reached a peak in August.
writing.explanation: peak 是高峰。reach a peak 是圖表常用語。
choices: reach to a peak of the

writing.example: The number hit a low in February.
writing.explanation: hit a low 表示降到低點。

writing.example: Prices remained stable for most of the year.
writing.explanation: remain + 形容詞 stable。

writing.example: The figure stood at 20 percent in 2015.
writing.explanation: stand at 用來報一個當時的數字。

writing.example: Food accounted for a third of their spending.
writing.explanation: account for 表示佔（比例）或解釋原因。

writing.example: The figures were 10 and 12 percent respectively.
writing.explanation: respectively 表示前面兩個數字各自對應。

speaking.cue: Do you like your hometown?
speaking.model: I come from a small city in the south of Taiwan. What I like most is the night market, because the food is cheap and friendly.

speaking.cue: What do you do?
speaking.model: At the moment, I'm preparing for IELTS. I mainly study in the evening, because I work during the day.

speaking.cue: How often do you use your phone?
speaking.model: To be honest, I use it pretty much all day. I mainly use it for messages and maps.

speaking.cue: What do you do to stay healthy?
speaking.model: I try to walk for thirty minutes after dinner. I've also cut down on sweet drinks.

speaking.cue: What is your favourite food?
speaking.model: My favourite is beef noodle soup. The reason is that it tastes rich but it is still a simple meal.

speaking.cue: What is the weather like in your country?
speaking.model: It depends on the season. For example, summer is hot and wet, while winter is milder in the south.

speaking.cue: Do you like listening to music?
speaking.model: I tend to listen to music on the metro. It helps me relax before work.

speaking.cue: Do you like reading?
speaking.model: I'm more of a news reader than a novel reader. I usually read for twenty minutes before bed.

speaking.cue: Do you prefer to spend time with friends or alone?
speaking.model: It depends. On the one hand, I like a quiet evening alone. On the other hand, I enjoy dinner with close friends.

speaking.cue: What do you usually do in the morning?
phrases: The first thing I do is...
speaking.model: The first thing I do is check the weather. After that, I have breakfast and leave for work.

speaking.cue: Do you like shopping?
speaking.model: Not really. I only shop when I need something, because crowded shops make me tired.

speaking.cue: Do you often go to parks?
speaking.model: I try to go once a week. It's a chance to walk and to get away from my desk.

speaking.cue: Why are you learning English?
speaking.model: I'm hoping to get band 6.5. The main reason is that I want to use English at work, not only in class.

speaking.cue: How do you usually travel to work or school?
speaking.model: I usually take the metro. It's more reliable than driving, and I can read on the way.

speaking.cue: What do you usually do at the weekend?
speaking.model: At the weekend, I cook and sometimes meet a friend. If I have time, I go to a market.

speaking.cue: Do you like taking photos?
speaking.model: I take photos of food and streets, but I don't spend long editing them.

speaking.cue: Describe a city you would like to visit.
speaking.model: I've always wanted to visit London. The main reason is that I could use my English in real shops and stations, and I would like to see the old buildings.

speaking.cue: Describe a person who helped you.
speaking.model: I want to talk about my English teacher. What I remember most is that she told me to answer first and then give one example. I felt much calmer after that.

speaking.cue: Describe a special meal you had.
phrases: One meal that stands out is...
speaking.model: One meal that stands out is a birthday dinner at a night market. It was special because my friends paid, and we stayed talking for two hours.

speaking.cue: Describe a quiet place you like.
phrases: The place I'd like to describe is...
speaking.model: The place I'd like to describe is the library near my office. I go there when I need to read. It is quiet because phones are not allowed.

speaking.cue: Describe a skill you would like to learn.
phrases: A skill I'd like to learn is...
speaking.model: A skill I'd like to learn is cooking simple healthy food. I'd start by learning three dishes. I want this skill because I eat out too often.

speaking.cue: Describe a trip you enjoyed.
speaking.model: Last year I went to Kenting with two friends. The best part was the train ride along the coast, because we talked the whole way.

speaking.cue: Describe a book or article you enjoyed.
speaking.model: I recently read a short article about walking. What I learned was that thirty minutes a day is enough to start. I read it because I wanted a simple health plan.

speaking.cue: Describe a job you would like to have.
speaking.model: The job I'd like is a junior designer in a small office. It suits me because I like clear tasks, and I would still have a colleague to learn from.

speaking.cue: Describe a gift you received.
speaking.model: The gift was a simple dictionary. A friend gave it to me when I started English. It mattered because I still use the notes I wrote in it.

speaking.cue: Describe your home.
phrases: The room I like most is...
speaking.model: I live in a small flat near a market. The room I like most is the kitchen, because it gets the morning light.

speaking.cue: Describe a phone app you often use.
speaking.model: My go-to app is a map. It's handy because I can check the metro even when I am in a new part of the city.

speaking.cue: Describe a busy day you had.
phrases: I had a busy day when...
speaking.model: I had a busy day when I worked and then studied for a test. By the end, I was tired but pleased, because I finished both.

speaking.cue: Describe a shop you like.
speaking.model: There's a small fruit shop near my building. I like it because the seller remembers what I usually buy.

speaking.cue: Describe a sport or exercise you do.
speaking.model: The exercise I do is walking. I do it because it does not need special shoes, and I can start from my front door.

speaking.cue: Describe a film you liked.
speaking.model: The film was about a student moving to a new city. I liked it because the story was simple and the ending was hopeful.

speaking.cue: Describe a teacher who influenced you.
speaking.model: One teacher who influenced me spoke slowly and waited. Because of that, I was less afraid to answer, even when my English was short.

speaking.cue: Why do many young people leave their hometowns?
speaking.model: The main reason is that big cities offer more jobs. On top of that, young people want a more exciting life. As a result, some towns become older.

speaking.cue: Who should protect the environment, governments or individuals?
speaking.model: In my view, governments play the main role, because they can make laws. At the same time, ordinary people should recycle and use public transport.

speaking.cue: Do children spend too much time on technology?
speaking.model: I'd say that many children do. On the one hand, technology can help them learn. On the other hand, they may stop playing outside.

speaking.cue: Is online learning better than classroom learning?
speaking.model: Both have pros and cons. The biggest advantage of online learning is flexibility. However, in a classroom you can ask questions at once.

speaking.cue: Why do many people find it hard to stay healthy?
speaking.model: The main reason is that modern life is busy, so fast food is easy. One solution is a short daily walk, which does not need a gym.

speaking.cue: What are the advantages of living in a city?
speaking.model: First of all, cities have more jobs and hospitals. However, rents are high, so the advantages do not help everyone equally.

speaking.cue: How can travel help young people?
speaking.model: First of all, they have to plan things themselves, so they become more independent. Another benefit is that they may use a foreign language.

speaking.cue: Is it better to work from home or in an office?
speaking.model: It depends on the job. For example, quiet writing is easier at home, but a new worker learns faster beside a colleague.

speaking.cue: Do advertisements have too much influence?
speaking.model: To a certain extent, yes. The problem is that some adverts make ordinary products seem necessary, especially to young people.

speaking.cue: Should museums be free?
speaking.model: I think they should be free on some days. The reason is that a free morning lets students visit, while the shop can still raise money.

speaking.cue: Are exams a good way to measure learning?
speaking.model: Exams can check knowledge quickly. However, they do not show speaking or teamwork, so a mix of coursework and exams is fairer.

speaking.cue: How can cities help older people?
speaking.model: One way is to build small flats near clinics. Another way is to support lunch clubs, so people are less isolated.

speaking.cue: Should cities invest more in public transport?
speaking.model: I strongly believe they should. For instance, a train every ten minutes can cut traffic, and it is cheaper than building more roads.

speaking.cue: Should schools control what students eat?
speaking.model: Schools can offer fruit and fewer sweet drinks. At the same time, parents still decide breakfast, so the school should not control everything.

speaking.cue: Should phones be banned in meetings?
speaking.model: A sensible rule is to put phones away in ordinary meetings. However, if a client needs to see a photo, a short exception is reasonable.

speaking.cue: Why is housing expensive near universities?
speaking.model: The main reason is that too many students want a short commute. The government could add low-cost beds and give first-year students priority.
